citations.B1: two requests can both pass the check before either increments, over-admitting
citations.B3: use a per-user lock or an atomic increment (e.g. `Lock`, `itertools.count`, or a `threading`-safe counter/Redis `INCR`)
citations.B4: No time window — once a user hits `limit` they're blocked forever, not per minute/hour
citations.B5: `counts` grows unboundedly for every distinct `user_id` seen, with no eviction — memory leak
citations.B6: separate worker processes (gunicorn/uwsgi workers) each get their own `counts`, so the real limit is `limit * num_workers`
citations.B7: No input validation on `user_id` — `None`, unhashable types, or malicious values aren't guarded
